sources.entry: mu - Open-source coding agent with a CLI and a desktop app, in which a small judge model makes routine calls such as what enters the context and whether a flagged command was asked for. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/qybaihe/mu) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: mu is an MIT-licensed coding agent built on pi, with a CLI and desktop app, that hands about 40 routine yes/no decisions (context admission, command approval, completion checks) to a small judge model.
summary.what_it_does: It wraps the pi coding agent with a judgment kernel that sends bounded questions to a small, fast judge model at 40 named decision points in the agent loop. Decision points cover what enters the prompt, trimming repeated test-log output, approving or refusing commands, screening web and MCP output for prompt injections, and checking whether a run actually finished. Each decision point can be active, shadow (logged only) or off, and every verdict is written to a local ledger with probabilities and timing. The default judge is the hosted Jev model; mu also supports a local mude 1.0 model on Apple silicon Macs, OpenAI's decision model, Hugging Face models, classifier models and any LLM, chained in tiers. It also includes a multi-subagent "hive" with a shared findings board and a plain-language progress board.
use_cases: run a coding agent in the terminal with fewer approval prompts
reduce token use from long test logs and tool output
screen web pages and MCP output for prompt injection
continue Claude Code or Codex CLI conversations in another agent
run a local decision model on a Mac for coding agent decisions
coordinate several subagents working on one codebase
how_to_run: npm i -g mu-agent # Node.js 22.19 or newer
mu # start a session in the current directory
mu doctor # check the installation, the judges and the connections
notable: A small judge model answers bounded yes/no, choice and score questions at 40 decision points, with a probability for each answer
Shadow mode records what a judge would decide without acting on it, for comparing judges before switching
Local ledger of every verdict, viewable via mu ledger, /status or the desktop app's Judge tab
Reported Terminal-Bench 2.1 result: 68.2% of attempts passed versus 58.7% for pi, on one Mac with a single model (self-reported)
Lossless folding of exact repeats in failing test logs, with the full log kept on disk
caveats: The local mude 1.0 setup supports only Macs with Apple silicon (macOS 14 or later, 8 GB memory or more); other platforms need a manual System One server setup
With no key set, the default Jev judge runs free on OpenCode Zen for a limited time, and judged content goes to OpenCode, which the README says does not train on it
Benchmark numbers are self-reported by the authors and were measured on one Mac with Rosetta, which the README says lowers absolute pass rates
keywords: agent that checks its own work
